Capability.meaning: Explicit operation grant on a resource or permission scope.

PrincipalGroup.meaning: Direct membership in a configured role or user group; a group can itself be a member. Supplied by trusted configuration or an authoritative identity source, never inferred from an agent-chosen name.

ResourceGroup.meaning: Permission-scope membership; grants on a parent apply to its descendants.

InGroup.meaning: Direct or nested role/user-group membership from PrincipalGroup. Membership alone is not permission.

Can.meaning: Grant including declared principal and resource memberships; not final authorization.

Field.meaning: Host-observed field or association of an application object or event. The binding defines cardinality, value type, fixed unit and optional observation-time field; never agent claims or hidden policy decisions.

Event.meaning: An event observed by the host, with its ID, actor and kind; recording it does not imply permission or success.

scope: Captured gate inputs and mediated callbacks. Outcomes follow the trusted adapter's confirmation contract; they are not independent proof of business success or authentic identity. Unmediated channels and missing observations remain outside this trace.

parameters.items: [{"action":"Re-cut the 2026-11-02 8-K (revenue, gross margin, December-quarter guide, FY2026 buyback) and the FY2026 10-K (other liabilities, intangibles, segment margin) into financials, thesis, scoring and the executive briefing, and restate the normalised free cash flow on audited FY2026 figures. If the documents cannot be obtained before delivery, say so in the executive briefing in one sentence: data stops at 2026-10-30, the 2026-11-02 print and 10-K are unread, and confidence in the margin normalisation and in the $270 entry trigger is medium rather than medium-high.","evidence_request":"FY2026 Q4 8-K of 2026-11-02 (revenue, gross margin, EPS, December-quarter guidance, buyback) and the FY2026 10-K (other current and non-current liabilities note, intangibles note, segment gross margin).","issue":"The report is cut at 2026-10-30 and reviewed on 2026-11-23, but three sections name the FY2026 fourth-quarter results and 10-K of 2026-11-02 as the decisive test: the executive briefing calls it 'the first hard test', thesis makes the $270 entry conditional on 'December confirms the margin trough', and scoring lists the 10-K working-capital note as open diligence. That print has been public for three weeks and is not in the report. The gap is decision-relevant, not cosmetic: the December-quarter gross-margin guide is the single input that decides between the 47-48% base and the 46% case that produces the entry price, and the audited FY2026 accounts would settle the intangibles/other-liabilities question the report flags as the soft spot in free cash flow.","sections":["executive_summary","financials","thesis","scoring","risk"],"severity":"Critical"},{"action":"Name four specific checks with the question each answers: Srouji's succession and retention award under the 2026-04-20 remit; Ternus's operating scope outside hardware; the general-counsel handover from Adams to Newstead while the DOJ and DMA cases are live; the 2026 equity awards to non-Section 16 SVPs.","evidence_request":"","issue":"The section says the 2024-26 turnover cluster 'is the part a reference check should attack' but names no referee or record to check, so the reference-check requirement in the team checklist is asserted rather than specified.","sections":["team"],"severity":"Minor"},{"action":"Pull the 2026 13G/A filings (due annually by mid-February) or label the KPI row '2023-12-31, not current' so the reader does not take a 2023 stake for a 2026 one.","evidence_request":"Current Schedule 13G/A holdings for Vanguard and BlackRock in Apple, filed 2026.","issue":"The cap-table KPI row carries BlackRock at 7.10% from a Schedule 13G/A reflecting holdings at 2023-12-31, three years stale, and Vanguard at 9.63% on the same basis, so the 'who owns Apple' line is partly a 2023 register.","sections":["company_overview"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: Completeness checklist, section by section. Company overview: single share class with par value and vote, entity table with all subsidiaries wholly owned, no VIE, 1977-2026 timeline dated to the day, liquidation preferences and anti-dilution not applicable (no preferred), board composition and committee chairs named — standard met. Team: education table with a sourced degree only where one exists, career table with dates, pay benchmarking against Nadella and Pichai, retention structure, key-person concentration on Srouji, and an explicit list of what is not disclosed; the only gap is named referees. Technology: patent table exists but carries no verified patent number — the section states this openly and downgrades confidence, which is the correct treatment rather than an omission. Market: TAM/SAM/SOM built bottom-up and cross-checked against two research houses, six regions with barriers and competitors, 'why now' tied to the memory shock; regional market values are missing and are already covered by a user data request. Competition: per-product map plus substitutes and status quo. Business model: per-device waterfall, cash conversion cycle, toll-by-toll treatment of the two contested revenue lines. Financials: three-year statement set, bridge to normalised free cash flow, returns and working-capital table, sensitivity block. Valuation: five methods, WACC grid, peer table with the Samsung/Xiaomi gap stated. Strategy, risk, thesis, exit, ESG, scoring all meet their component requirements (risk-matrix and info; scenarios and analogs; sensitivity and takeaways). Automated check on version 1: no rule findings, no depth or layout findings, all fourteen sections above the 2,500-character floor (range 5,366-8,991). No report-level completeness finding from me. One structural observation: the same three facts (50.1% margin less two points of refunds, $20bn search payment, $122.6-127.3bn normalised FCF band) carry the argument in nine sections; that is legitimate for a conclusion but it means an error in any one of them propagates, which is why the three number items in passes 2 and 5 matter out of proportion to their size.

OpenAI (and xAI) are absent as adjacent entrants although risk cites their suit, and Meta appears only in a wearables positioning row; vivo, OPPO, Honor and Transsion are named as competitors in market but never in competition; and the memory suppliers who set the 2026 margin appear only as a cost line, not as a party with pricing power over Apple.","sections":["competition","market","technology_product"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Add Epic Games and alternative storefronts to the competitor table as distribution rivals, with the DMA fee schedule and the link-out ruling as their entry subsidy.","evidence_request":"","issue":"Epic Games, the DMA-enabled alternative marketplaces and Spotify as a distribution rival appear in ESG and business_model but not in the competitive landscape, although they are the mechanism by which the services take rate is being repriced.","sections":["competition"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: Competitors considered and found: Samsung (present, unit leader, loss-making mobile), Huawei (present, China leader, HarmonyOS scale), Xiaomi (present), Google (present, and supplier), Lenovo/HP/Dell (present for PC), Spotify (present), Alphabet advertising (present), status quo (present). Considered and missing: OpenAI and its reported device work; Meta's AI glasses; xAI; vivo, OPPO, Honor and Transsion (named elsewhere); Epic and alternative stores; Sony and Nintendo (console adjacency, immaterial to Apple's profit pool); Qualcomm (modem supplier being insourced, correctly framed as a cost item rather than a rival); TSMC and the memory makers (supply concentration, not competition, but the memory makers set Apple's 2026 margin and deserve a row); academic spin-outs and open-source (no credible open-source phone OS threat; Android is already the free substitute and is listed). Geographic blind spots within the table as written: China is covered through Huawei only, India and Africa only through the market section, and no Latin America rival.

parameters.items: [{"action":"Decompose the 22.4% nine-month iPhone growth and the 12-14% services assumption into units, price/mix and installed-base growth, using the active-device series and any disclosed paid-subscription or upgrade data, and state what the 2.5bn base figure assumes. Add one paragraph on the price step as the sell: at what price the SE/18e buyer defects, and what carrier financing absorbs.","evidence_request":"Apple's active-device count and any upgrade-rate or paid-subscription disclosure from the FY2026 Q4 call and 10-K; carrier instalment terms for the iPhone 18 Pro.","issue":"The report flags its own hardest question (units versus price) but never answers it: there is no installed-base growth rate, upgrade rate or paid-subscription count, so the 22.4% iPhone growth, the 12-14% services forecast and the per-device economics all rest on one undated 2.5bn active-device figure. A price-led cycle and a user-led one have different terminal values, and the report cannot tell which it is buying.","sections":["market","business_model","technology_product"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Add the per-device split for services (attach rate, paid subscriptions, ARPU) and state who approves the price step in the channel: carrier instalment plans and the upgrade-cycle length.","evidence_request":"","issue":"The buyer of the $1,199 handset is identified as the consumer on carrier financing, but the channel mechanics are never tested: instalment duration, upgrade-cycle length and trade-in support are what make a 27.6% ASP increase sellable, and they are absent.","sections":["business_model","market"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: The five PMF questions, answered from the report as written. Hardest thing about selling: not the device but the price step — memory-driven ASPs are up 27.6% while units fall 16.7%, and Apple has no second price point until the spring 2026 iPhone 18 (partly addressed in technology and market). Budget owner: the consumer, financed through the carrier; services are bought by the subscriber and the developer, and the report says so once without testing it. Sales cycle: annual September launch plus a spring cycle from 2027 — well evidenced. Why adoption is not faster: Siri AI entered beta only on 2026-09-14, 23 months after Apple Intelligence, and the foldable is a first generation — the report gives the mechanism. Lost deals: never asked. The report has no account of a buyer who chose Huawei, Samsung's foldable or a longer device life, and the status-quo row in competition is the only proxy. That is the gap worth closing: the price elasticity of the $1,199 buyer is the single assumption that decides whether FY2026 is a peak.

parameters.notes: Stress arithmetic. Gross margin: base 48.1% less memory pass-through. At 46% FY2027 EPS is $9.3 and value is $270 at 29x, $229 at 24.6x — the entry price becomes the fair value, so a two-point miss removes the margin of safety entirely and the call survives only as 'do not own'. Search payment: at $25bn the ban case is about -16% of EPS and roughly -$44 a share at 29x, enlarging the bear to about $200-215. EPS: 8% below $9.79 gives a base of $261 and a weighted $272 (-21%), which deepens the call but does not flip it. Weights: 15/50/35 gives $280 and -19%. DCF: 9.5% costs $193, 8.5% gives $229; the market needs 7.0%, so even the most generous defensible rate leaves the price 34% above intrinsic — the discount rate, not growth, is the whole question, and the report says so. Market cap: on 14,697.9m shares the multiple is 40.4x normalised free cash flow and 39.5x trailing, so the two published figures bracket the arithmetic error. Installed base: at 2.2bn devices per-device revenue is $212 and per-device R&D $19.5; nothing in the conclusion moves. Balance sheet: the 30% revenue fall case (EPS $5.4, $95bn operating income) is survivable on $62.2bn of net cash, and a 30% free-cash-flow fall still covers the buyback but not dividends. Every stress tested leaves the direction of the call intact; the ones that matter change the entry price and the base case anchor, not the rating.
